= Check Advisory Reports

A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that polls all draft security advisories in this repository and verifies that each one conforms to the https://github.com/spring-projects/security-advisories?tab=readme-ov-file#creating-report[reporting requirements].
If any advisory fails validation, the workflow fails and annotates each issue in the Actions log.

[[validation-rules]]
== Validation Rules

Each draft advisory body is checked against three rules.

[[validation-rules-required-sections]]
=== Required Sections

Every advisory must contain all six of the following `###` headings:

* `### Summary of the CVE`
* `### Advisory Checklist`
* `### Instructions on running the minimal sample`
* `### Instructions on reproducing the issue`
* `### Describe the expected result`
* `### Describe the actual result and explain why it is a vulnerability`

[[validation-rules-checklist-items]]
=== Checklist Items

Every `* [ ]` or `- [ ]` task-list item found in the body is treated as an unchecked checklist item and reported as a failure.
All items must be marked `[x]` before the advisory is considered ready.

[[validation-rules-section-content]]
=== Section Content

The following sections must contain real prose — content that remains after HTML comments are stripped must be non-empty:

* `### Summary of the CVE`
* `### Instructions on running the minimal sample`
* `### Instructions on reproducing the issue`
* `### Describe the expected result`
* `### Describe the actual result and explain why it is a vulnerability`

The `### Advisory Checklist` section is exempt from this check because its value is captured by the <<validation-rules-checklist-items,checklist item rule>>.

[[permissions]]
== Required Permissions

The workflow requires the `repository-advisories: write` permission so that the GitHub token can list draft advisories and update their title and description via the GitHub REST API.
This is declared explicitly on the `check` job in the workflow file.

[[usage]]
== Usage

Two workflows support this script.

[[usage-triage]]
=== Triage Security Advisories (`triage-security-advisories.yml`)

Runs the script against all draft advisories and updates their titles and descriptions.
Triggers:

* **Daily at 08:00 UTC** — the scheduled poll that catches advisories filed or edited since the last run.
* **Manual dispatch** — trigger a run at any time from the Actions tab.

[[usage-test]]
=== Test Triage Security Advisories (`test-triage-security-advisories.yml`)

Runs the JavaScript test suite to verify the script is correct.
Also used as a reusable workflow — `triage-security-advisories.yml` calls it before running triage to ensure tests pass first.
Triggers:

* **Pull request targeting `main`** — runs on every PR regardless of which files changed.
* **Push to `main`** — when the workflow file or any file under `.github/scripts/triage-security-advisories/` changes.
* **`workflow_call`** — called by `triage-security-advisories.yml` before triage runs.

No additional configuration is required.
Both workflows read `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` from the standard GitHub Actions environment.

[[usage-example]]
=== Example Workflow Output

A conforming advisory produces a single info line, and no advisory changes are written:

----
✓ GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz conforms to requirements
----

A non-conforming advisory annotates each failure as an error, then updates the advisory:

----
::error::GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz: Missing required section: "### Summary of the CVE"
::error::GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz: Unchecked checklist item: * [ ] The expected result
Updating advisory GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz...
----

After the run, the advisory title is prefixed with `PENDING: ` and its description gains a status block showing the failures.
Once all issues are resolved the prefix is removed and the status block is updated to PASSING on the next run.
Only advisories whose title or description actually changed are written back to the API.

[[development]]
== Development

[[development-prerequisites]]
=== Prerequisites

* https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm[nvm] — the correct Node.js version is declared in `.nvmrc`.

[[development-running-tests]]
=== Running Tests

[source,shell]
----
cd .github/scripts/triage-security-advisories
nvm use
npm ci
npm test
----

Coverage report:

[source,shell]
----
npm run test:coverage
----

[[development-project-structure]]
=== Project Structure

[cols="1,3"]
|===
| File | Purpose

| `src/security-advisory-triage.js`
| Pure validation logic; stateless functions with no I/O.

| `src/advisory-status.js`
| Builds and updates the status block embedded in the advisory description.

| `src/advisories.js`
| `Advisories` class — wraps `@octokit/rest` to list and update draft advisories.

| `src/index.js`
| Entry point — reads environment variables, orchestrates the check, updates titles and descriptions, and reports results via `@actions/core`.

| `tests/security-advisory-triage.test.js`
| Unit tests for every validation rule and helper function.

| `tests/advisory-status.test.js`
| Unit tests for status block construction and idempotency.

| `tests/advisories.test.js`
| Unit tests for `listDraftAdvisories` using `vi.mock` to stub `@octokit/rest`.

| `tests/advisories-update.test.js`
| Unit tests for `updateAdvisory` using `vi.mock` to stub `@octokit/rest`.
|===
